words.gloss_range: said, with local force as an externalized speech act introducing direct quotation
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, speech, and opinion; the direct quotation selects outward speech rather than inner opinion
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) turns the narration into a live speech turn: a completed Form I saying is routed to the servant before Mūsā is named, then it opens the whole permission-and-teaching request as one quotation. The word is simple in form, but its placement makes discipleship begin as spoken consent rather than silent pursuit, while same-surah speech echoes near (18:60) and the guidance request at (18:10) keep this utterance inside the surah's request-for-direction field.

topics.headline: completed speech opens a directed quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins not with movement or learning but with a completed speech act aimed at the servant and enclosing the whole request.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment evidence force {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) as a perfect reporting verb with dative addressee, delayed explicit subject, and quoted complement over words 4-11.

topics.headline: bare Form I lets the request carry the weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb simply opens outward speech, leaving the humility and stipulation to appear inside the quotation rather than in a heavier speech form.
topics.reason: The local direct-speech scope selects utterance from the broader {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) range, and Form I does not add causative or intensified force.

topics.headline: speech joins following, teaching, and guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speech verb is not a neutral tag; it initiates the consent-dependent chain of following, teaching, and guidance, with a same-surah dialogue reopening at (18:60).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect the opening speech to local following and teaching roots and to same-surah speech frames; attachment evidence confirms that the following words are the quoted content.

topics.headline: open vowels mark the frame before the request tightens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a gentle acoustic separation between the spacious reporting frame and the denser request that follows.
topics.reason: The sound observation is locally tied to the three-word speech frame and does not conflict with the syntactic analysis.

words.gloss_range: to him, locally the dative addressee of the speech verb
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, relation, adjacency, and authority; locally narrowed by the preposition-plus-pronoun function to directed address
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) makes the servant the addressee before the verse names Mūsā. The attached pronoun carries the servant forward from (18:65), so the request is already relational and accountable to the one addressed, and it opens the encounter's recurring pattern of speech moving between Mūsā and the servant. Its broader nearness field is only a color here; local grammar makes the word a dative address, not possession. The light l-h sound also works as a soft hinge between the speech verb and the named speaker.

topics.headline: the servant receives the speech before Mūsā is named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the servant's role as consulted addressee is foregrounded before the speaker's name appears.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the suffix in {{ar:لَهُ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) the addressee of {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}), and cross-reference evidence resolves it to the servant introduced in (18:65).

topics.headline: relational nearness colors but does not replace dative address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word directs speech into a relationship of nearness and consultation while grammar still keeps the sense as address, not ownership.
topics.reason: The wider {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) relation field can supply color, but the local preposition after a speech verb fixes the operative function as dative address.

topics.headline: pronoun binding keeps the dialogue compact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not reintroduce the servant by name; a bound pronoun carries the prior scene into the new dialogue turn.
topics.reason: The suffix is definite and referential; it compresses addressee continuity from the previous ayah into one dependency word.

topics.headline: the address pattern starts a reciprocal dialogue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this addressee anchor begins the encounter's repeated pattern of speech moving between Mūsā and the servant.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify a local dialogue thread; the attachment evidence supports the current word as the opening addressee anchor.

topics.headline: light sound mediates verb and name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the small pronoun as an audible hinge between the speech verb and the named speaker.
topics.reason: The phonetic claim is modest and locally anchored in the three-word speech frame.

words.gloss_range: Mūsā, a foreign proper name functioning by reference rather than Arabic-root derivation
words.prose: {{ar:مُوسَىٰ}} ({{tr:mūsā}}) resolves the delayed subject of the speech frame and prevents the servant-pronoun from being mistaken as the speaker. Because the name is a foreign proper noun, its force is narrative identity rather than root semantics: the well-known prophet appears here as petitioner, follower, and potential student, a reversal sharpened by comparison with Mūsā-following scenes such as (7:142) and (26:52). Across the boundary, divine bestowal gives way to human petition: the searcher now asks for access to what was given.

topics.headline: the name locks the speaker after the addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause first establishes the servant as addressee, then names Mūsā as the one making the request.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies {{ar:مُوسَىٰ}} ({{tr:mūsā}}) as the explicit subject of {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}), placed after the dative addressee.

topics.headline: foreign proper-name force overrides root play
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word contributes the identity of Mūsā, not an Arabic lexical branch to be mined for local sense.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a foreign proper noun; the final written shape supports transmitted-name behavior rather than Arabic derivation.

topics.headline: a dominant prophet takes the student position
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the role inversion: the frequent prophetic actor becomes the one asking to follow another human teacher.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows locate the payoff in narrative distribution and role reversal; local syntax confirms Mūsā as requester inside the quotation.

topics.headline: the searcher becomes the asker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary shift from divine bestowal and search narrative to Mūsā's human petition for access to what was given.
topics.reason: The preceding ayah introduces the servant's divine teaching, while the present speech frame has Mūsā request entry into that received knowledge.

words.gloss_range: yes-no interrogative particle, locally functioning as a polite permission request
words.prose: {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) makes Mūsā's first quoted word a question, so the proposed following depends on the teacher's permission. The particle keeps both forces alive: it asks whether following may happen, and by doing so it preserves the servant's right to refuse before any teaching begins. Its clipped shape gives the quoted request a sharp onset before the proposal unfolds into following and condition.

topics.headline: question form makes the request permission-seeking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā does not command or presume access; his grammar makes permission the first content of the request.
topics.reason: QAC allows the particle as interrogative and polite request marker; translation support warns against rendering the question as a bare command.

topics.headline: the particle launches an ordered proposal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the request unfolding in sequence: permission, following, and then the teaching condition.
topics.reason: The quoted complement begins at {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}), and the following attachment chain connects it to the conditional proposal.

topics.headline: brief particle gives the request a clear onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how a short particle sharply marks the move from narrative frame into deferential request.
topics.reason: The surface brevity and pragmatic force are locally tied to the opening of the quoted request.

words.gloss_range: may I follow you, locally a proposed ongoing, voluntary discipleship relation with the servant as direct object
words.root_gloss_range: following, coming after, tracking, pursuit, and adherence; local condition selects disciplined following for instruction, not hostile pursuit or desire-following
words.prose: {{ar:أَتَّبِعُكَ}} ({{tr:attabiʿuka}}) makes Mūsā the first-person actor, but his action is chosen subordination: he asks to place himself after the addressed servant. The Form VIII shape and object suffix make the following voluntary and personal, while the following ʿalā an condition makes it conditional on teaching. The root's wider tracking and adherence range is narrowed here to discipleship, especially against desire-following in (18:28) and in contrast with the follow-to-guidance pattern in (40:38). The doubled t sound makes the requested close attachment audible.

topics.headline: following takes the servant and a teaching condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that following is not bare movement; it is a personal relation governed by a teaching condition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the suffix the direct object and {{ar:عَلَىٰ أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿalā an}}) the governed condition for the following verb.

topics.headline: Form VIII makes following self-undertaken
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā's humility is active: he chooses to enter the follower position rather than being made to follow.
topics.reason: The imperfect first-person Form VIII supports prospective self-involvement; it contrasts with a causative made-to-follow frame.

topics.headline: the object suffix binds following to one teacher
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā asks to follow the person addressed, not merely a path, doctrine, or abstract knowledge.
topics.reason: The attached {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) is the direct object and resolves to the addressed servant.

topics.headline: tracking imagery becomes teachable discipleship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete image of going behind someone on a course, while the teaching condition narrows that image to apprenticeship rather than chase or surveillance.
topics.reason: The broader {{ar:ت ب ع}} ({{tr:t-b-ʿ}}) range is real, but local grammar and the final guidance goal select disciplined following.

topics.headline: same root tests valid and invalid following
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this following belongs to a wider contrast: not desire-following in (18:28), but teacher-following ordered toward guidance, with the later condition in (18:70) testing it.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references and local root recurrence; none conflicts with the local parse.

topics.headline: gemination makes close following audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sound pressure that suits the semantic pressure of close attachment behind the teacher.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the actual surface and is used as secondary support.

words.gloss_range: upon, on the condition that; locally the preposition introducing the teaching condition
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) is the hinge that makes following rest on a term: Mūsā asks to follow on the basis that the servant teach him. It is not simple coordination, so the request does not mean follow plus separately learn; the teaching clause is the condition that defines the following relationship.

topics.headline: following is built on a teaching condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā is not asking for proximity alone; he frames the relationship around instruction as its condition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) govern the {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) teaching clause as the condition for {{ar:أَتَّبِعُكَ}} ({{tr:attabiʿuka}}).

topics.headline: upon-sense gives the stipulation weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relationship is pictured as resting on a stated term, while grammar keeps the local sense as conditional rather than spatial location.
topics.reason: The particle's literal pressure can color the condition, but local syntax governs a verbal complement rather than a physical object.

topics.headline: preposition replaces simple and
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that following and teaching are not equal side-by-side actions; the second clause defines the terms of the first.
topics.reason: The syntax uses prepositional linkage rather than coordination, preserving the hierarchy between following and being taught.

words.gloss_range: that, to; locally a subordinator governing the following subjunctive teaching verb
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the teaching action into a dependent clause under the condition introduced by ʿalā. The small particle carries large syntactic force: it makes teaching prospective, conditional, and grammatically tied to the proposed following rather than an asserted fact.

topics.headline: the teaching verb is made dependent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the teaching is not guaranteed or reported; it is grammatically suspended inside Mūsā's proposed condition.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence show {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) governing {{ar:تُعَلِّمَنِ}} ({{tr:tuʿallimani}}) in a dependent subjunctive clause.

topics.headline: the particle supplies the verbal content of the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that teaching is both the term and the aim of following, not an unrelated second request.
topics.reason: After {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), the subordinator lets the following verb phrase function as the content of the condition.

topics.headline: a small hinge opens the teaching unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the transition from the proposed act of following into the inner clause that gives the request its substance.
topics.reason: The structural and sound rows are locally coherent: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) both begins the dependent teaching unit and binds audibly to the following verb.

words.gloss_range: that you teach me, locally causative Form II teaching with the servant as teacher and Mūsā as learner
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, teaching, informing, signs, marks, and landmarks; local Form II selects causing to know, while mark/landmark imagery can color the teaching
words.prose: {{ar:تُعَلِّمَنِ}} ({{tr:tuʿallimani}}) is the center of the request: the addressed servant is encoded as the one who teaches, and Mūsā is encoded as the one taught. Form II makes the request causative, closer to make me know than merely tell me, while the source phrase and final rushdan give that teaching a received source and a right-direction goal. The mark-and-landmark edge of the root colors teaching as orienting marks left on the learner, while local grammar keeps caused knowing as the selected sense; the compressed first-person ending still keeps Mūsā present as object. Its echo with ʿullimta and the divine teaching of (18:65) makes the verb a relay point, not an isolated lesson, and the repeated root cadence with the doubled consonant makes that causative relay audible. The request also looks ahead to the capacity test in the next exchange.

topics.headline: teacher, learner, source, and goal gather around the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb organizes the whole epistemic tail: who teaches, who receives, from what source, and toward what guidance.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence supplies Mūsā as object, the partitive source phrase, and the final guidance object or specification, all dependent on {{ar:تُعَلِّمَنِ}} ({{tr:tuʿallimani}}).

topics.headline: teaching remains requested, not asserted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the teaching is still contingent inside the proposal, not already granted.
topics.reason: The verb is governed by {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}), so its mood keeps the transfer prospective.

topics.headline: Form II asks the teacher to cause knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā asks for the teacher's active causative role, not simply for himself to learn on his own.
topics.reason: The local Form II pattern selects causative teaching from the broader {{ar:ع ل م}} ({{tr:ʿ-l-m}}) range and contrasts with learner-centered alternatives.

topics.headline: mark and landmark imagery colors teaching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that teaching can be imagined as leaving orienting marks on the learner, while local grammar keeps caused knowing as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The mark/sign branch belongs to the supplied root field, but the local Form II verb and object relation select teaching; the image survives as orientational color.

topics.headline: recitational forms expose Mūsā as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the compressed final object still keeps Mūsā grammatically present as the one to be taught.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the protective nūn and first-person object, and the variant rows expose rather than alter that role.

topics.headline: active teaching mirrors received teaching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a relay: what God taught the servant in (18:65) becomes what Mūsā asks the servant to teach him in (18:66).
topics.reason: The same root and Form II recur across the boundary and locally in active/passive pairing, while the syntax makes the servant a transmitter.

topics.headline: sound binds causative teaching to reception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated root cadence and doubled consonant as an audible counterpart to causative teaching and received teaching.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows are tied to the same local Form II active/passive sequence and are kept as secondary payoff.

topics.headline: the request prepares a capacity test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request to be taught will immediately be tested by whether Mūsā can bear the knowledge in the next exchange.
topics.reason: The forward bridge is concrete and local to the following response, so it can survive as an anticipatory discourse payoff.

words.gloss_range: from what, locally a fused partitive source phrase for what is to be taught
words.root_gloss_range: bestowal, gift, obligation, and manna in the wider field; locally narrowed because the surface functions as min plus mā, with gift-field pressure secondary
words.prose: {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) limits the request to a portion from what the servant was taught. Its fused form makes source and unspecified content one unit, then waits for ʿullimta to define the what; the nasal cadence binds the partitive source and passive reception as one audible unit before the final guidance word. The gift field of {{ar:م ن ن}} ({{tr:m-n-n}}) is narrowed here: it colors the portion as a bestowed share, while grammar keeps the operative meaning as partitive source, echoing the prior min-pattern of (18:65).

topics.headline: Mūsā asks for a share, not all knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the humility of partition: the request draws from the servant's received knowledge without claiming the whole of it.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) as the partitive source complement of the teaching verb.

topics.headline: from and what fuse into a dependent source unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word creates controlled incompleteness: from what is left open until the passive clause resolves it.
topics.reason: The surface parses as min plus mā, and the following passive verb supplies the relative content.

topics.headline: gift language colors the partitive share
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested portion feels like a share from prior bestowal, while the local particle still means from what.
topics.reason: The supplied {{ar:م ن ن}} ({{tr:m-n-n}}) field supports bestowed-share color, but the local word is structurally min plus mā rather than an independent gift noun.

topics.headline: the partitive repeats the prior ayah's extraction pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuity from the divine giving of (18:65) to Mūsā's measured request in (18:66): knowledge moves by portions, not possession.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows name the prior ayah's min-pattern and the current partitive source; the echo is concrete and locally relevant.

topics.headline: nasal sound binds source to passive reception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the fused partitive and passive source as one audible unit before the final guidance word lands.
topics.reason: The phonetic payoff supports the same source dependency already established by grammar.

topics.headline: portion, source, and goal form the ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final movement from a portion, to its received source, to the kind of guidance sought.
topics.reason: The word pivots from the teaching verb to the passive source phrase and sets up the final specification.

words.gloss_range: you were taught, locally a perfect passive Form II marking prior received teaching
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, teaching, informing, marking, signs, and landmarks; local passive Form II selects caused reception of knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:عُلِّمْتَ}} ({{tr:ʿullimta}}) resolves the source phrase by saying that the servant was already taught. The perfect passive makes him a prior recipient before he can become Mūsā's teacher, and it leaves the teaching agent unspoken even though (18:65) has already supplied the divine source. Its Form II echo with tuʿallimani turns the clause into a relay: received knowledge can be transmitted onward only as received knowledge. A secondary marking image lets the servant appear marked by knowledge, while the rare passive form and doubled consonant foreground caused reception rather than ordinary knowing.

topics.headline: the teacher is first a taught recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the servant's authority is grounded in prior reception, not self-originating knowledge.
topics.reason: QAC and implicit-argument evidence make the addressee the passive patient in a perfect Form II verb.

topics.headline: the passive leaves the teacher's Teacher unspoken
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices reverent deagentivization: the servant is foregrounded as recipient while the ultimate giver remains grammatically unexpressed.
topics.reason: The passive form leaves the agent unexpressed, and the prior ayah (18:65) provides the background for divine teaching without requiring the agent to be named here.

topics.headline: caused reception replaces simple knowing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form says the servant was made to know, not merely that he knew or originated teaching.
topics.reason: The passive Form II blocks both a simple knowing reading and an active teacher-origin reading.

topics.headline: active request mirrors passive reception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the three-tier chain: God taught the servant, the servant may teach Mūsā, and the requested content is right direction.
topics.reason: The same Form II root appears in active request and passive reception, with the partitive source phrase connecting them.

topics.headline: the passive completes from what
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) becomes a received-knowledge source only when this passive verb arrives.
topics.reason: The relative source phrase depends on the passive verb for completion and then points forward to the guidance goal.

topics.headline: passive marking image remains secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a possible image of knowledge marking the servant, while the selected local sense remains being taught.
topics.reason: The mark branch is part of the root field, but local morphology and syntax select passive teaching as the operative meaning.

topics.headline: rare passive form and sound foreground reception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the passive reception form stands out inside a common knowledge root and is audibly compacted by the Form II pressure.
topics.reason: The distributional and phonetic claims reinforce the same locally forced passive-reception analysis.

words.gloss_range: right direction, guidance, sound judgment; locally the requested guidance as object, specification, or state
words.root_gloss_range: right guidance, maturity, sound judgment, upright course, and opposition to error; local context selects teachable right direction while retaining maturity and judgment pressure
words.prose: {{ar:رُشْدًۭا}} ({{tr:rushdan}}) gives the request its final goal: not information in general, but right direction. Its accusative can be heard as taught content, specification, or state, so the word is a grammatical hinge as well as the ayah's closing destination, and its indefinite verbal-noun form keeps the goal an open-ended quality to be taught rather than a named doctrine. The root field includes maturity and sound judgment, as in (4:6), and stands against error as in (2:256); in this line that range is narrowed to teachable right orientation, a course to travel behind the teacher. Accepted vowel variation thickens the maturity-versus-course range without changing that local goal. The word is linked to the surah's guidance moments at (18:10) and (18:24) and tested by the patience issue that follows in (18:67).

topics.headline: one accusative supports object, specification, and state readings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word can name what is taught, the respect in which teaching happens, or the state sought in following, with local syntax favoring taught guidance.
topics.reason: QAC permits tamyīz, direct object, and state readings; attachment evidence strongly licenses it as the guidance taught, so alternatives survive as qualified grammatical pressure.

topics.headline: guidance includes maturity and sound judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Mūsā is asking for right orientation and developed judgment, not a neutral transfer of facts.
topics.reason: The broader {{ar:ر ش د}} ({{tr:r-sh-d}}) range includes maturity and sound judgment, but the teaching context selects guidance as the local operative sense.

topics.headline: right course joins the following verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance feels like a course to be traveled behind the teacher, not merely a concept to hear.
topics.reason: The local following verb and final guidance noun make the route image coherent, with a concrete follow-guidance comparison at (40:38).

topics.headline: indefinite verbal noun keeps the goal qualitative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested guidance is an open-ended quality or state to be taught, not a named doctrine or fixed item.
topics.reason: The maṣdar-like form and tanwīn support qualitative openness while still functioning in the teaching clause.

topics.headline: variant vowels expose range without changing the goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted vowel variation thickens the maturity-versus-course range while the local request still lands on right guidance.
topics.reason: The variant rows illuminate semantic range but do not replace the aligned local surface or its syntactic role.

topics.headline: Surah 18 threads guidance requests together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word belongs to a Surah 18 guidance thread linking the sleepers' prayer (18:10), the instruction to seek nearer guidance (18:24), and Mūsā's request here.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete same-surah references and the recurrence is directly relevant to the word's local sense.

topics.headline: the final word prevents generic knowledge-seeking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends by narrowing received knowledge into the specific requested outcome of right direction.
topics.reason: The word is final and tied to the teaching verb, so it defines the destination of the request rather than adding optional decoration.

topics.headline: guidance request anticipates the patience test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request for right direction immediately raises the question whether Mūsā can receive it with patience in (18:67).
topics.reason: The forward bridge names the next ayah's response and is relevant to the teachability implied by the request.

baseline_models.mechanism: A spoken proposal joins following to teaching under a stated condition, forming an asymmetrical apprenticeship whose end is sound conduct rather than information alone.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation over a matter makes the opening question a proposed apprenticeship compact.
Following and imitation supply the subordinate teacher-learner relation.
Disclosure to a knower makes teaching the intended transfer within that relation.
Sound handling of an affair gives the transfer a practical, conduct-shaping end.

changed_reading.before: Moses asks a knowledgeable person for useful information.
changed_reading.after: Moses proposes entering a governed apprenticeship in which following is the condition for acquiring sound practical judgment.

baseline_models.mechanism: Following can be a slow tracing of successive signs; teaching then cultivates recognition of marks that disclose a straight course.

activation_trace.role: Tracing one mark after another turns following into an investigative method.
A distinguishing mark that guides makes taught knowledge legible as signs.
The straight-path image gives those signs a directional end away from error.

changed_reading.before: Guidance is an abstract answer delivered by a teacher.
changed_reading.after: Guidance is wayfinding competence acquired by following and learning to read discriminating marks.

baseline_models.mechanism: The active and passive teaching forms place the teacher inside a prior chain of disclosure, while مِمَّا asks for a share rather than exhaustive possession.

activation_trace.role: The same disclosure image governs both the teacher's prior receipt and the requested onward teaching.
Sound disposition limits the requested share by an operative end rather than total knowledge.

changed_reading.before: The addressee owns a body of knowledge that he may transmit.
changed_reading.after: The addressee is an intermediate recipient asked to relay a fitting portion of what first reached him.

context_deltas.mechanism: Before the request, reaching the sought encounter requires reversing course and tracking an enduring trace. The journey therefore gives concrete procedural force to the focus model of following as sign-reading.

activation_trace.role: Stepwise tracing is the focus-ayah method that the preceding journey enacts.
Returning something to its place supplies the reversal needed after passing the sought point.
A remaining sign of what was there makes prior footprints usable evidence.
Tracking an أثر supplies the actual procedure by which the encounter is recovered.

structural_cues: 18:61-64 sequences missed sign, recognition, reversal, and close retracing before 18:65's encounter.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies return, residual marks, and trace-tracking; I infer that this outer search prefigures the requested learning method. A live alternative is that it only localizes the encounter in the plot.

changed_reading.before: Following a teacher may cultivate wayfinding in principle.
changed_reading.after: Moses asks to learn by the same discipline just enacted: notice what was missed, reverse when necessary, and recover the way from residual traces.

context_deltas.mechanism: Following becomes a temporal discipline: lack of encompassing inside-knowledge must be borne without immediate interrogation until the teacher elects to disclose the matter.

activation_trace.role: Following and imitation provide the relation whose conditions are subsequently specified.
Holding the self back from distress makes restraint, not passive duration, the learner's burden.
Complete cognitive enclosure names the knowledge the learner presently lacks.
Knowledge of a matter's interior distinguishes experienced grasp from surface reaction.
Making a thing manifest assigns the timing of disclosure to the teacher.

structural_cues: 18:67-68 ties inability to patience to lack of encompassing خبر.
18:70 makes following conditional on withholding questions until teacher-initiated mention.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-encompassment, restraint, and teacher-timed disclosure; I infer a pedagogy in which premature questions freeze a still-unfolding event. Alternatively, the prohibition may be only contract management rather than a teaching method.

changed_reading.before: Following supplies proximity in which questions can obtain guidance.
changed_reading.after: Following first requires disciplined exposure to what cannot yet be encompassed; questioning becomes legitimate only after the event has ripened for disclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The acts arrive in sequence before their intelligibility; only at separation are they reported back to their outcomes. Teaching thus works retrospectively, converting endured anomalies into causal judgment.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure to the knower anchors the later explanation as fulfillment of the requested teaching.
Distinguishing and separating mark the threshold at which companionship gives way to explanation.
News that arrives and is conveyed supplies the delayed explanatory report.
Return to a matter's outcome relocates meaning from first appearance to eventual consequence.
One thing following another makes the ordered succession of episodes part of the explanatory form.

structural_cues: 18:71-77 repeats act, objection, and warning three times before 18:78 announces separation and تأويل.
18:79-82 then reorder each troubling appearance by disclosing its consequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delayed news, outcome-return, and sequential episodes; I infer a didactic arrow from enacted anomaly to retrospective intelligibility. A live alternative is that the closing account is merely a defense of the acts.

changed_reading.before: Teaching precedes action by stating the rule that should guide it.
changed_reading.after: Teaching may stage opaque action first and disclose its rule through consequences only afterward, so sequence and delay are themselves instructional.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus passive 'you were taught' expands into a delegated chain: the teacher is identified through obedient servanthood, receives knowledge from beyond himself, and denies acting from his own authority.

activation_trace.role: Prior disclosure to the teacher anchors the focus request in received rather than self-originated knowledge.
Submissive obedience makes the knowledgeable guide accountable within a higher relation.
Explicit teaching from 'Us' resolves the focus passive as a prior grant of knowledge.
Authority and its holder clarify the denial that the acts arose from the teacher's own command.

structural_cues: 18:65 frames the teacher as one of 'Our servants' and both mercy and knowledge as grants 'from Us.'
18:82 denies that the actions were done from the teacher's own command.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies received knowledge, servant status, and non-self-originated command; I infer that authority constrains both the content and exercise of what can be taught. Alternatively, these clauses may describe status and action without defining pedagogy.

changed_reading.before: Moses asks an expert to share a portion of his expertise.
changed_reading.after: Moses asks entry into a delegated trust: the guide may transmit and enact only what he himself has received under authority.

context_deltas.mechanism: The explanations align sound disposition with protection across time: damage blocks coercive seizure, substitution averts a feared burden, and stored wealth remains covered until unsupported children reach strength. Timing, concealment, and controlled release become dimensions of rushd.

activation_trace.role: Sound handling of an affair, including mature disposition, anchors the focus request in competent stewardship.
Coercive unjust seizure makes apparent impairment function as protection of vulnerable workers' property.
One thing standing in place of another supplies a future-oriented remedy rather than restoration of the first state.
Children cut off from a caretaker identify the dependency that requires custodial delay.
Preserved stored wealth supplies the asset kept inaccessible for its owners.
Reaching full strength fixes the future threshold for rightful release and use.

structural_cues: 18:79 explains a visible defect by the confiscation it prevents.
18:80-82 couple feared future harm and protected orphan wealth with substitution, maturity, and delayed access.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three future-directed protections; I infer a common custodial arrow in which limited present harm or withholding preserves a vulnerable interest. Alternatively, the three explanations may exemplify distinct judgments without one fiduciary model.

changed_reading.before: Rushd is general right guidance or prudent choice.
changed_reading.after: Rushd is timed custodial judgment: discern whose interest is exposed, what must be withheld or altered now, and when protected agency or property can safely emerge.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it shifts saying and teaching from verbal delivery toward material semiotics. It remains anchored in the focus branches for a thing's indicative 'speech' and a guiding mark, while the context supplies altered objects and delayed manifestation. Render it as an exploratory pedagogy of signs, not as a denial of the later verbal explanation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قَالَ ... تُعَلِّمَنِ, read through القول as indication and العلم as a distinguishing mark

activation_trace.role: A thing's indication as its 'saying' permits nonverbal states to carry intelligible testimony.
A distinguishing mark that guides makes material alteration potentially instructional.
Later manifestation preserves the teacher's eventual act of making the marked matter explicit.
A literal breach supplies a conspicuous negative mark whose purpose is initially unreadable.
Restoring straightness supplies a contrary material mark whose hidden function also awaits explanation.

changed_reading.before: Moses asks to hear explanatory instruction while accompanying the teacher.
changed_reading.after: Moses may be asking to learn a language of events in which altered things first 'say' through marks and receive verbal exposition only later.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation is branch-distant because it uses the عيلم image of abundant gathered water under the focus root علم. It remains packet-anchored through the double علم and the immediately preceding confluence of two seas. Render it only as a material analogy for the requested portion of knowledge, never as the primary lexical sense of the focus verbs.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ, activated by the علم branch of abundant water gathered in an عيلم

activation_trace.role: Abundant water gathered in a sea or well recasts received knowledge as pooled depth.
Joining what was separate into one gathered thing supplies the confluence that activates the water image.
Wide abundant water gives the contextual material analogue for the focus branch.

changed_reading.before: Teaching transfers a bounded item of knowledge from one mind to another.
changed_reading.after: The request may image teaching as drawing a navigable share from gathered depth at a confluence, with following needed to move through rather than exhaust it.

strongest_changes: Following becomes retracing: missed signs, reversal, and residual footprints define a method of learning.
Patience becomes epistemic restraint under non-encompassment until teacher-timed disclosure.
Teaching becomes retrospective: sequential anomalies are returned to their outcomes only at separation.
Rushd becomes timed custodianship of vulnerable interests, agency, and stored property.
summary.what_was_special: The focus roots interlock unusually tightly with the pericope's form: ت ب ع is enacted as trace-following, the two علم forms become a delegated relay and a mark-reading practice, and the orphan-treasure ending concretizes the practical-disposition branch of رشد.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether delayed questioning is intrinsically pedagogical or only a condition for this companionship.
Whether the three final explanations support one custodial mechanism or several irreducible judgments.
The material-speech and gathered-water readings are packet-licensed analogies but remain branch-distant and should stay explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Following is proposed as the medium of learning.** `ت ب ع` B001 (“following after”) precedes teaching and right guidance. Dhul-Qarnayn later follows a supplied means to successive limits (18:85, 89, 92), showing following as disciplined path-use. I infer that knowledge here requires temporal submission to another’s sequence, not extraction of answers on demand. Moses correctly requests apprenticeship before repeatedly violating its pacing.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The repeated following of means at 18:85, 89, and 92 widened apprenticeship into a general path-to-endpoint grammar.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Guidance sought as practical judgment, not route information.** `ر ش د/B001` is guidance on a straight course; `ر ش د/B002` is sound judgment in handling an affair. The request joins following to teaching, and within five ayat the boat is pierced (18:71), an act whose practical rightness cannot be read from its surface. I infer that the desired `رُشْدًا` is the capacity to map visible damage to a wider affair. The ayah reads as apprenticeship in causal judgment rather than acquisition of directions.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:67–70 defined the requested judgment procedurally, and 18:71 supplied the first act whose visible defect resists surface evaluation.

Bir kişi, olay veya bilginin bıraktığı iz ve belirtileri tek tek inceleyerek ilerlemek.
Bir kimsenin kusurlarını veya geride bıraktığı kayıt ve nesneleri ayrıntılı biçimde araştırmak.

root_profile.summary: Kök, bir kişi veya şeyin ardından gitme çekirdeğinden yetişme, aşamalı iz araştırması, kesintisiz ardışıklık, hak isteme ve kişide kalan yük gibi ilişkilere açılır; ayrıca sığır yavrusu, tarihsel hükümdar unvanı, doğaüstü eşlikçi ve belirli kalite yapıları gibi sözlükselleşmiş dallar taşır. Duyusal nesne etiketi altında toplanan gölge, beden bölümü, yıldız, kuş ve böcek adları tek üretken anlam gibi genellenmeden sınırlı adlandırmalar olarak tutulur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dalın bilme ve bilgisizliğin karşıtı olma yönündeki çekirdeği kaynak ifadesiyle uyumludur. Ancak haberden haberdar olma, öğretme, öğrenme ve bilgi bakımından üstün gelme kullanımları bu çekirdekle aynı düzeyde değil, belirli biçimlere bağlı uzantılar olarak tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak bilme çekirdeğini öne alır; haber, öğretim, öğrenim ve karşılıklı bilgi sınamasıyla ilgili anlamları yalnızca ilgili biçim ve kuruluşlara bağlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bilmek, tanımak ve onu gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavramak; böylece bilgisizlikten çıkmaktır. Haber verilmesi, öğretme, öğrenme ve bilgi bakımından üstün gelme bu çekirdekten hareket eden, belirli biçimlere bağlı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.
Bir haberin farkına varmak veya ondan haberdar olmak, bilme çekirdeğinin belirli bir konuya uygulanmasıdır.
Bildirme, öğretme ve öğrenme biçimleri bilginin bir başkasına ulaştırılması ya da kişinin onu edinmesi süreçlerini anlatır.
Karşılıklı bilgi sınamasında birini yenmek, belirli bir kuruluşta ortaya çıkan rekabetçi kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği, bilgiyi bilgisizliğin karşıtı sayar ve bir şeyi tanıyıp gerçeğiyle kavramayı öne çıkarır. Toplu tanıklık ayrıca haberden haberdar olmayı, bilgiyi aktarmayı, öğrenmeyi ve bilgiyle üstün gelmeyi biçime bağlı uzantılar olarak gösterir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi başkasından ayıran belirgin izi dalın ortak çekirdeği olarak açıkça destekler. Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş deseni ve savaş işareti gibi örnekler bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir; tanınmış kişi ve son zaman belirtisi ise benzetme veya gösterme ilişkisine bağlı uzantılardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ayırt edici iz çıplak çekirdektir; savaşçı, kumaş, sarık ve belirli zaman göstergesiyle kurulan anlamlar kendi kuruluşlarına bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başkalarından ayıran, tanınmasını sağlayan veya ona götüren belirgin iz ya da işarettir. Bayrak, uzaktan seçilen dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş kenarı ve sonradan konan tanıtıcı izler bu işlevin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi veya kişiyi başkalarından ayırıp tanınır kılan belirgin iz ya da işaret çekirdeği oluşturur.
Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi ve kumaşın kenar deseni yön bulduran veya tanıtan somut gerçekleşmelerdir.
Savaşçının, kumaşın veya sarığın ayırt edici bir işaretle donatılması belirli kuruluşlara bağlı eylemsel kullanımdır.
Tanınmış bir kişinin belirgin bir bayrağa benzetilmesi ve yaklaşan son zamanı gösteren belirti, işaret çekirdeğinin uzantılarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ayırt edici izi ortak temel sayar ve bayrak, yüksek ya da belirgin dağ, yol göstergesi, kumaş kenarı, kına ve sonradan yerleştirilen tanıtıcı işaretleri bu temelde toplar. Tanınmış kişi ile yaklaşan son zamanın belirtisi de görünürlük ve gösterme işlevinden doğan uzantılardır.
